jobs.title: Drift Wood #22 · still there
jobs.prompt: a four-panel comic strip laid out as a two-by-two grid on a half page, thin black panel borders (4 panels). Style: black and white comic strip panel, scratchy crow-quill pen and ballpoint ink on cardstock, harsh photocopy contrast, heavy black spotting, jagged uneven line weights, 1990s indie comix zine style, xerox grain, no color, no gray tones. Cast, drawn the same in every panel, ages exactly as given: WOOD — aged 18, gaunt boy drawn a head too tall, oversized thrift-store wool overcoat to the knee worn indoors, faded black tee, dark jeans, sneakers, a bristol pad clutched flat to his chest, chin up; CHLOE — aged 18, girl with a sharp intelligent face, smudged heavy black eyeliner, straight dark hair to the shoulders, oversized dark cardigan, a Discman on her belt with headphones around her neck, a folded-back paperback, reads while talking. Title of the strip: DRIFT WOOD. The strip: Two weeks later the envelope has moved. It has not been opened. Panel 1: a teenage girl with a stack of newspaper proofs in a bedroom doorway, a boy at a drawing table with an envelope pinned under a jar of pens (in this panel: CHLOE, WOOD). Chloe says "Proofs. You're late. What's under the jar?". Panel 2: close-up of a hand sliding a jar of pens to cover more of an envelope on a drawing table (in this panel: WOOD). Wood says "Reference material.". Panel 3: a teenage girl in a doorway reading an envelope's return address from across the room, narrow-eyed, a boy at the table looking away (in this panel: CHLOE). Chloe says "Reference material from the Pacific Northwest College of Art.". Wood says "They send those to everyone.". Panel 4: a teenage boy alone at a drawing table lifting a jar off an envelope, looking at it, and setting the jar back down, proofs on the bed behind, no words (in this panel: WOOD). No dialogue in this panel. Lettering: every balloon and caption contains its complete text exactly as written, in clean hand-lettered comic capitals, large enough to read; size each balloon to fit its whole sentence and never cut a word at a balloon or panel edge; no words other than the ones given. Bottom right margin: tiny signature "A. Finch — Small Wood, OR" beside a tiny stylized gull, two strokes. Reference @chloe_17 is the model sheet for CHLOE: match that face, build, hair and clothes exactly. Reference @gully_17 is the model sheet for GULLY: match that face, build, hair and clothes exactly. Reference @wood_20 is the model sheet for WOOD: match that face, build, hair and clothes exactly. Match the attached references: @chloe_17 for the character the strip's Chloe at 17; @gully_17 for the character the strip's Gully at 17; @wood_20 for the character Wood at 20-23.
